title: Survival priorities (Rule of 3s)
text:
1. Remember the Rule of 3s: about 3 minutes without air, 3 hours without shelter in harsh weather, 3 days without water, 3 weeks without food.
2. Work in that order: protect breathing, then shelter from heat, cold, or rain, then water, then food — and signal for rescue throughout.
3. When in trouble, S.T.O.P.: Stop, Think, Observe, Plan. Panic is the first killer — sitting still for 5 minutes is often the best first move.
4. Stay where rescuers can find you, unless staying is more dangerous (fire, flood, ashfall, gunfire).
5. From the start, ration your phone battery, water, and energy — assume rescue takes days, not hours.
source: US Army Field Manual FM 21-76 (Survival) / NDRRMC

title: Mga prayoridad sa survival (Rule of 3s)
text:
1. Tandaan ang Rule of 3s: mga 3 minuto nang walang hangin, 3 oras nang walang silungan sa masamang panahon, 3 araw nang walang tubig, 3 linggo nang walang pagkain.
2. Sundin ang pagkakasunod: protektahan ang paghinga, saka silungan laban sa init, lamig, o ulan, saka tubig, saka pagkain — at sumenyas ng rescue sa lahat ng oras.
3. Kapag nasa gipit, S.T.O.P.: Hinto, Mag-isip, Magmasid, Magplano. Ang panic ang unang pumapatay — ang pag-upo nang 5 minuto ay kadalasang pinakamagandang unang galaw.
4. Manatili kung saan ka mahahanap ng rescuer, maliban kung mas delikado ang manatili (sunog, baha, ashfall).
5. Sa simula pa lang, tipirin ang baterya ng cellphone, tubig, at lakas — isiping aabutin ng araw, hindi oras, ang rescue.
source: US Army Field Manual FM 21-76 (Survival) / NDRRMC

title: Finding water in the wild
text:
1. Collect rain first: spread clean plastic, cloth, or big leaves to funnel rain into containers.
2. At dawn, wipe dew from grass and metal with a clean cloth and wring it into a container.
3. Tie a clear plastic bag over a leafy branch — by afternoon the sun pulls drinkable vapor inside (transpiration bag). Avoid foul-smelling or milky-sapped plants.
4. Follow clues downhill: green vegetation, birds, bees, and animal tracks often lead to water. Dig in damp hollows of dry stream beds.
5. NEVER drink seawater, urine, or alcohol — all dehydrate you faster. Purify everything you collect (see purifying_water).
source: US Army Field Manual FM 21-76 (Survival) / WHO Water Safety

title: Paghahanap ng tubig sa wild
text:
1. Sahurin muna ang ulan: ilatag ang malinis na plastik, tela, o malalaking dahon para padaluyin ang ulan sa lalagyan.
2. Sa madaling-araw, punasan ng malinis na tela ang hamog sa damo at metal at pigain sa lalagyan.
3. Itali ang malinaw na plastic bag sa madahong sanga — pagsapit ng hapon, hihilahin ng araw ang maiinom na singaw sa loob (transpiration bag). Iwasan ang mabaho o magatas na halaman.
4. Sundan ang mga palatandaan pababa: luntiang halaman, ibon, bubuyog, at bakas ng hayop ay kadalasang patungo sa tubig. Humukay sa mamasa-masang bahagi ng tuyong sapa.
5. HUWAG kailanman uminom ng tubig-dagat, ihi, o alak — mas mabilis itong nakaka-dehydrate. Linisin ang lahat ng makolekta (tingnan ang purifying_water).
source: US Army Field Manual FM 21-76 (Survival) / WHO Water Safety

title: Making wild water safe to drink
text:
1. Strain cloudy water through a clean cloth first — all methods work better on clear water.
2. Best method: rolling boil for at least 1 minute, then cool covered.
3. No fire, sunny day: fill a clear plastic bottle three-quarters, shake 20 seconds, lay in full sun for 6 hours (2 days if cloudy).
4. Or bleach: 2 drops of unscented bleach per liter of clear water, mix, and wait 30 minutes. A slight chlorine smell is normal.
5. Drink in small frequent sips and prioritize children, elderly, and the sick.
source: WHO / DOH Water Safety Guidelines

title: Paglilinis ng tubig mula sa wild
text:
1. Salain muna ang malabong tubig sa malinis na tela — mas epektibo ang lahat ng paraan sa malinaw na tubig.
2. Pinakamaganda: pakuluan nang kumukulo nang hindi bababa sa 1 minuto, saka palamigin nang nakatakip.
3. Kung walang apoy at maaraw: punuin ng tatlong-kapat ang malinaw na plastic bottle, alugin nang 20 segundo, ibilad sa araw nang 6 oras (2 araw kung maulap).
4. O bleach: 2 patak ng walang pabangong bleach kada litro ng malinaw na tubig, haluin, at hintayin ng 30 minuto. Normal ang bahagyang amoy ng chlorine.
5. Uminom nang paunti-unti pero madalas, at unahin ang bata, matanda, at maysakit.
source: WHO / DOH Water Safety Guidelines

title: Making a campfire safely
text:
1. Prepare BEFORE striking: a bundle of dry tinder (shredded bark, dry grass), kindling (twigs), and fuel (sticks) — in a clear, wind-sheltered spot away from tents and trees.
2. Build teepee-style: tinder in the center, kindling around it, and light from the side the wind blows from. Feed slowly — smothering kills young flames.
3. Keep matches and lighters dry in a sealed container, and always carry two ways to make fire.
4. NEVER leave a fire unattended. Keep water or soil beside it at all times.
5. Extinguish fully: drown with water, stir the ashes, feel for heat — if too hot to touch, repeat until cold.
source: US Army Field Manual FM 21-76 (Survival) / Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP)

title: Paggawa ng campfire nang ligtas
text:
1. Maghanda BAGO magsindi: bungkos ng tuyong tinder (pinunit na balat ng kahoy, tuyong damo), kindling (maliliit na sanga), at gatong (kahoy) — sa malinis na lugar na protektado sa hangin, malayo sa tent at puno.
2. Ayusin nang parang teepee: tinder sa gitna, kindling sa paligid, at sindihan mula sa gawing nanggagaling ang hangin. Pakainin nang dahan-dahan — namamatay ang batang apoy kapag natabunan.
3. Panatilihing tuyo ang posporo at lighter sa saradong lalagyan, at laging magdala ng dalawang paraan ng pagsisindi.
4. HUWAG kailanman iwanang walang bantay ang apoy. Magtabi ng tubig o lupa sa lahat ng oras.
5. Patayin nang lubusan: buhusan ng tubig, haluin ang abo, kapain ang init — kung masyadong mainit hawakan, ulitin hanggang lumamig.
source: US Army Field Manual FM 21-76 (Survival) / Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP)

title: Building an emergency shelter
text:
1. Choose the site first: high, dry, flat ground. NEVER in dry riverbeds (flash floods), under dead lone trees, or in hollows where cold air pools.
2. Insulate from the ground above all: a thick bed of dry leaves, grass, or spare clothes — the ground steals body heat fastest.
3. Simplest builds: a tarp or plastic lean-to tied between trees, or a debris hut (branch frame piled thick with leaves). Block the wind and trap body heat.
4. Stay near open ground so rescuers and your signals stay visible.
5. In rain, dig a small drainage trench around the bed and keep all gear off the ground.
source: US Army Field Manual FM 21-76 (Survival) / NDRRMC

title: Paggawa ng emergency shelter
text:
1. Piliin muna ang lugar: mataas, tuyo, patag na lupa. HUWAG sa tuyong ilog (flash flood), sa ilalim ng patay na nag-iisang puno, o sa lubak na pinamumugaran ng malamig na hangin.
2. Unahin ang insulation mula sa lupa: makapal na higaan ng tuyong dahon, damo, o reserbang damit — pinakamabilis magnakaw ng init ng katawan ang lupa.
3. Pinakasimpleng gawin: tarp o plastik na lean-to na itinali sa mga puno, o debris hut (balangkas ng sanga na tinambakan ng dahon). Harangin ang hangin at kulungin ang init ng katawan.
4. Manatili malapit sa bukas na lugar para kita ka at ang mga senyales mo ng rescuer.
5. Kapag umuulan, humukay ng maliit na kanal sa paligid ng higaan at ilayo sa lupa ang lahat ng gamit.
source: US Army Field Manual FM 21-76 (Survival) / NDRRMC

title: Signaling rescuers (seen and heard)
text:
1. The universal distress call is anything in THREES: 3 whistle blasts, 3 flashes, or 3 fires in a triangle — repeated every minute.
2. By day: flash a mirror or shiny metal toward aircraft, boats, or ridges; make dark smoke with green leaves on a fire to show against the sky.
3. By night: a bright flame or flashlight is visible for kilometers. Keep one light always ready.
4. Make big contrasting ground marks: SOS letters, an X (need help), or branch-and-stone arrows pointing your direction — readable from the air.
5. Wear or wave your brightest clothing. Once you have signaled, stay put (see no_signal_sos) — moving hides you from searchers.
source: US Army Field Manual FM 21-76 (Survival) / NDRRMC

title: Pagsenyas sa rescuer (kita at rinig)
text:
1. Ang universal distress call ay kahit ano na TATLO: 3 pito, 3 kislap, o 3 apoy na tatsulok — inuulit kada minuto.
2. Sa araw: kumislap ng salamin o makintab na metal papunta sa eroplano, bangka, o burol; gumawa ng maitim na usok gamit ang sariwang dahon sa apoy para kita sa langit.
3. Sa gabi: kita nang kilometro ang maliwanag na apoy o flashlight. Maghanda ng isang ilaw sa lahat ng oras.
4. Gumawa ng malalaki at matingkad na marka sa lupa: letrang SOS, X (kailangan ng tulong), o arrow na sanga at bato papunta sa direksyon mo — nababasa mula sa himpapawid.
5. Isuot o ikaway ang pinakamatingkad na damit. Kapag nakapag-senyas na, manatili sa puwesto (tingnan ang no_signal_sos) — nawawala ka sa searcher kapag gumagalaw.
source: US Army Field Manual FM 21-76 (Survival) / NDRRMC

title: Two rescue knots (bowline + clove hitch)
text:
1. Learn TWO knots before any trip: the bowline (a loop that will not slip — for rescue lines) and the clove hitch (a fast tie for shelter poles and tarps).
2. Bowline memory aid: 'the rabbit comes out of the hole, around the tree, and back down the hole' — then pull the loop hard to test it.
3. NEVER trust your weight to a newly learned knot — test it low to the ground first, and re-check after rain, because ropes loosen.
4. Practice at home until your hands tie both without thinking — cold, wet, shaking hands fumble everything new.
5. For rescue pulls, loop the bowline around the chest under the arms — never around the neck.
source: US Army Field Manual FM 21-76 (Survival) / Philippine Red Cross

title: Dalawang rescue knot (bowline + clove hitch)
text:
1. Matutuhan ang DALAWANG buhol bago umalis: bowline (silo na hindi dumudulas — para sa rescue line) at clove hitch (mabilis na tali para sa poste ng shelter at tarp).
2. Pantanda sa bowline: 'lumabas ang kuneho sa butas, umikot sa puno, at bumalik sa butas' — saka hilahin nang mariin ang silo para subukan.
3. HUWAG kailanman ipagkatiwala ang bigat ng katawan sa bagong-aral na buhol — subukan muna nang mababa sa lupa, at suriin ulit pagkatapos ng ulan, dahil lumuluwag ang lubid.
4. Mag-practice sa bahay hanggang kusang itinatali ng mga kamay ang dalawa — nagkakamali sa lahat ng bago ang malamig, basa, at nanginginig na kamay.
5. Sa paghila ng rescue, isilo ang bowline sa dibdib sa ilalim ng kilikili — huwag kailanman sa leeg.
source: US Army Field Manual FM 21-76 (Survival) / Philippine Red Cross

title: Finding direction without a compass
text:
1. Sun: it rises roughly in the east and sets roughly in the west. Face the sunrise — north is on your left, south on your right.
2. Stick-shadow trick: push a stick upright, mark the shadow tip, wait 15 minutes or more, mark it again — the line between the marks runs roughly west to east (first mark is west).
3. Night sky: find the Big Dipper and follow its edge stars to the North Star — it points to true north.
4. Water rule: follow streams downhill — settlements sit near water. Mark your path as you go so you can backtrack.
5. Do NOT trust moss on trees — it grows on any damp side and misleads. Trails and markers beat every trick.
source: US Army Field Manual FM 21-76 (Survival) / NDRRMC

title: Paghahanap ng direksyon nang walang compass
text:
1. Araw: sumisikat ito nang humigit-kumulang sa silangan at lumulubog sa kanluran. Humarap sa pagsikat — nasa kaliwa ang hilaga, nasa kanan ang timog.
2. Stick-shadow trick: itusok nang patayo ang patpat, markahan ang dulo ng anino, maghintay ng 15 minuto o higit pa, markahan ulit — ang guhit sa pagitan ay humigit-kumulang kanluran-silangan (kanluran ang unang marka).
3. Langit sa gabi: hanapin ang Big Dipper at sundan ang gilid nitong bituin papunta sa North Star — tumuturo ito sa tunay na hilaga.
4. Water rule: sundan ang sapa pababa — malapit sa tubig ang mga pamayanan. Markahan ang dinadaanan para makabalik.
5. HUWAG magtiwala sa lumot sa puno — tumutubo ito sa alinmang basang parte at nanlilinlang. Mas maaasahan ang trail at markers kaysa alinmang trick.
source: US Army Field Manual FM 21-76 (Survival) / NDRRMC

title: Wild food safety (what NOT to eat)
text:
1. Rule one: NEVER eat unknown plants, mushrooms, or berries — no exceptions. Old 'edibility tests' are unreliable and can kill.
2. You can survive weeks without food but only days without water — spend your energy on water and shelter first.
3. Eat only what you KNOW: coconut meat and water, bananas from known trees, fish you caught yourself — and cook all fish and meat thoroughly.
4. Avoid dead animals and foul-smelling water. When in doubt, go without — hunger will not kill you today.
5. If anyone feels sick after eating wild food (vomiting, dizziness, blurred vision), keep a sample of what was eaten and get to medical help fast.
source: WHO / DOH Food Safety Guidelines

title: Kaligtasan sa pagkain sa wild (huwag kainin)
text:
1. Unang panuntunan: HUWAG kailanman kumain ng hindi kilalang halaman, kabute, o berries — walang eksepsiyon. Hindi mapagkakatiwalaan ang lumang 'edibility tests' at nakamamatay ang mga ito.
2. Kayang mabuhay nang ilang linggo nang walang pagkain pero ilang araw lang nang walang tubig — ibuhos ang lakas sa tubig at silungan muna.
3. Kainin lang ang SIGURADO: laman at tubig ng niyog, saging mula sa kilalang puno, isdang ikaw mismo ang humuli — at lutuing mabuti ang lahat ng isda at karne.
4. Iwasan ang patay na hayop at mabahong tubig. Kung nagdududa, huwag kumain — hindi ka papatayin ng gutom ngayong araw.
5. Kung may sumama ang pakiramdam pagkatapos kumain ng wild food (pagsusuka, pagkahilo, panlalabo ng mata), magtabi ng sample ng kinain at magpatingin agad.
source: WHO / DOH Food Safety Guidelines

title: Animals at camp (snakes, monkeys, rats)
text:
1. Shake out shoes, clothes, and bags every morning and night — snakes and scorpions shelter inside them.
2. Store all food sealed and away from where you sleep. Never eat inside the tent.
3. Never feed monkeys or stray dogs — fed animals bite. Back away slowly; do not run or stare.
4. If you meet a snake: freeze, then back away slowly. Most bites happen when people try to catch or kill it (see snakebite).
5. Keep a light or small fire going at night and zip tents fully — light and noise deter most animals.
source: DENR Wildlife Guidelines / Philippine Red Cross

title: Mga hayop sa camp (ahas, unggoy, daga)
text:
1. Ipagpag ang sapatos, damit, at bag tuwing umaga at gabi — sumisilong sa loob ang ahas at alakdan.
2. Itago ang lahat ng pagkain nang sarado at malayo sa tulugan. Huwag kumain sa loob ng tent.
3. Huwag pakainin ang unggoy o gumagalang aso — nangangagat ang nasanay pakainin. Umatras nang dahan-dahan; huwag tumakbo o tumitig.
4. Kung makasalubong ng ahas: huminto, saka umatras nang dahan-dahan. Kadalasang nakakagat kapag sinusubukang hulihin o patayin ito (tingnan ang snakebite).
5. Panatilihing may ilaw o maliit na apoy sa gabi at isara nang husto ang tent — umiiwas ang karamihan sa hayop sa liwanag at ingay.
source: DENR Wildlife Guidelines / Philippine Red Cross
